judgments.reasoning_cat1: The execution date is left as "July ¥, 2005", so the "Effective Date" — a term on which the Employment Term, salary, commissions and severance all depend — has no legible day.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 1.9, 2.2(e), 2.2(f), 8.1 and 8.4 all measure entitlements from the Effective Date, an unfixed date could ripple through those provisions, though the year and month are clear enough to blunt most disputes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition naming a specific body; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1 refers to reporting to "the Board (or selected designee of the Board of Directors of the Parent)" and Schedule 2.1 to the Chairman, but the definition itself is consistent with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Business" is defined by a long enumerated list closed with "including but not limited to ... and other related services", a classic general catch-all against specifics whose reach is uncertain, and it is keyed to activities engaged in "at any time during the Employment Term".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This definition drives Article V(a)'s covenant not to compete and 1.6's "Core Business", and V(d)'s substitution of Core Business for Business only works if the two differ meaningfully — which the overlapping definitions make doubtful.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard statutory definition with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Code" is defined but appears nowhere else in the operative text, a harmless orphan rather than an inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "known to the Employee as a consequence of or through the Employee's employment" is vague at the edges, and the list of covered items has no temporal limit or invention carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with 4.1's assignment obligation (which covers items "conceived, developed or acquired during the Employment Term") and 4.2's assertion that all Company Technology is already Company property, a mismatch in scope.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "all information, in whatever form, regarding Parent, the Company their Business and their clients" is boundless and contains a missing comma; the ten enumerated categories sit against an "including, without limitation" catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exceptions live in 3.1 rather than the definition, so the definition alone would sweep in public-domain material; read with 3.1 the two harmonise reasonably well.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (b)(ii) is mathematically incoherent — revenue that must exceed the sum of 1% of consolidated revenue plus its own first-year revenue can never qualify — and "prior to the termination of employee" is garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because Article V(d) substitutes "Core Business" for "Business" as the post-8.4 restriction, the defect in this definition directly determines the scope of the surviving non-compete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (a) — "a client of the Parent, or of the Company or its subsidiaries" — has no temporal boundary at all, while (b) and (c) are carefully time-limited, leaving the reach of (a) contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Customer" is used only in Article V(b), where the unbounded limb (a) would extend the non-solicit to clients the Employee never knew, in tension with V(e)'s acknowledgment of reasonable scope.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is technical but reasonably determinate, though "as determined by reference to the components set forth in Ajuba's audited financial statements" and the accountants' resolution clause could be argued over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(b) times bonus payment off "the audited financial statements of Parent" while this definition keys EBITDA to Ajuba's audited statements, a mismatch of financial-statement source.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear commencement and end date; "third anniversary of this Agreement" is a slight variant of "Effective Date" but means the same thing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.1 uses "third anniversary of the Effective Date" and 1.14 measures the Restricted Period from the end of the Employment Term, so an early termination shortens the Term and thus the restriction — coherent but worth checking.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite calendar definition with a standard change mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(a) uses lower-case "fiscal year ending December 31, 2005" alongside the defined term, a trivial inconsistency only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names a specific corporation; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parent is given third-party beneficiary status in 9.9 and appears in 1.5, 1.7 and V(b); all consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "any corporation, company, partnership, other entity or individual" places a general catch-all after enumerated forms, but the reach is plainly universal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Person" is used only in 2.1(b) and 6.1; no tension found elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Geographically definite, although "territories and protectorates" is a slightly archaic descriptor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 1.2's "in the United States and India" and V(a), the area is coextensive with the Business; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Commencing at signature and ending three years after the end of the Employment Term yields up to a six-year restraint, an overbreadth a court would readily be asked to construe or reform.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with V(a)-(c), V(e)'s reasonableness acknowledgment and Article VII's judicial-modification sentence, which itself contemplates that these restrictions may be overbroad.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "such other legally permissible and proper duties" and "consistent with Employee's services provided to the Company prior to the date hereof or with Employee's position" are open-ended, and "Schedule 2.1 shall be deemed to have been amended" leaves the amendment's content unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the Employee reports directly to the Board while Schedule 2.1 says he "Reports to the Chairman of the Board", and its deemed-amendment cross-reference to 8.4(a) is the pivot of the Good Reason diminution test.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The EBITDA escalator is ambiguous: "retroactive to the first business day of the year following the Fiscal Year in which such EBITDA was achieved" combines retroactivity with a forward date, and it is unclear whether the $3.5m test applies once or in each year.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The $3.5m trigger duplicates the lowest 2005 bonus tier in 2.2(b) while 8.2/8.5 cut off "any other bonus or other compensation pursuant to Section 2", so entitlement on termination must be reconciled with those clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The tiers are discrete thresholds with no stated treatment of EBITDA falling between them, and "eligible to receive" sits uneasily with a fixed schedule; the final sentence's double negative about 8.3/8.4 termination is awkwardly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties payment to Parent's audited statements though 1.8 defines EBITDA off Ajuba's, and 8.2/8.5 deny any bonus while 8.3/8.4 preserve a prior-year Bonus — the interlock is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Entitlement to participate is immediately qualified by unlimited discretion to modify or discontinue, which is one-sided but not genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(a) gives an Allowance "in lieu of receiving health, dental and other benefits afforded to Ajuba US employees", which sits awkwardly with a general right to participate in all plans; 8.2-8.5 each cut off participation after termination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "substantially similar to the D&O Policy maintained by the Company immediately prior to the date hereof" is a soft standard but a familiar and workable one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses D&O cover; a 8.4(c) breach claim could rest on it, but nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Samii" is never identified, "net sales" is undefined, and the quoted phrase "goes live" has no definition; the employment condition is tied to a monthly "Payment Date" that is itself defined mid-sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 8.3 and 8.4 refer to the Reorganization Bonus as payable "in accordance with Section 2.2(e)", but 2.2(e) is this commissions clause and the Reorganization Bonus is 2.2(f) — a live cross-reference error.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "when and if" the UK office "is shut down" and the Novi office "is restructured" depends on Schedule I completion tests outside the Employee's control, and the payment date (twelve-month anniversary) may precede or follow completion with no stated rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 8.3 and 8.4 preserve the Reorganization Bonus by citing "Section 2.2(e)" rather than this subsection (f), and Schedule I disclaims any warranty of the very cost savings this clause says the Schedule "sets forth".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "reasonable out-of-pocket expenses" and "in accordance with Company policies" are standard and workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Breach of 2.3 is a Good Reason trigger under 8.4(c), which gives it teeth but creates no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition runs to disclosure "to any entity", which literally omits natural persons, and the exceptions are enumerated with no catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on the very broad 1.5 definition and is echoed by Exhibit A ¶5's continuing obligations; the pieces fit together adequately.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite return-and-delete obligation triggered by termination.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A ¶2 imposes a broader "Company Information and Property" return duty; the two overlap but do not contradict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "except for legitimate business purposes" is an unbounded exception that largely swallows the confidentiality promise, and the term is nowhere defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A ¶13 repeats the identical formula, so the same vagueness recurs; no direct conflict, but the Employee has no reciprocal freedom under 3.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assignment is triggered only "Upon the Company's request and to the extent permitted by law", and the clause covers inventions "relating in any way to the Business", a notably elastic phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.2 declares that all Company Technology "is and shall remain the property of the Company", which presupposes ownership that 4.1 says must still be assigned on request.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligations to return, not use, and delete are concrete; "now or hereinafter in the possession" is loose but familiar.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its premise that the Company already owns the Company Technology sits against 4.1's request-based assignment mechanic, the same tension viewed from the other side.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "engage in any activity which is in competition with the Business", "directly or indirectly" and the residual "or otherwise" after an enumerated list of capacities leave the covenant's reach genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its scope is set by 1.2, 1.13 and 1.14 (up to six years across two countries), altered by V(d), and duplicated in part by the separate Non-Competition Agreement preserved by 9.8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "accept from any Customer any such competitive business" bars even unsolicited business, and "any of their affiliates" extends to undefined third parties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It rests on the temporally unbounded limb (a) of the 1.7 "Customer" definition and runs for the 1.14 Restricted Period, so the outer boundary depends on definitions that are themselves loose.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "any employee in the United States or any employee in India having the title of Supervisor and above" is syntactically ambiguous as to whether the Supervisor qualifier attaches to US employees too, and the carve-out's repeated "the preceding sentence" is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The proviso is internally circular — general advertising is allowed provided no employee is hired in violation of the same sentence — but nothing elsewhere contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The substitution is a single mechanical sentence, but its effect turns entirely on whether "Core Business" is narrower than "Business".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Under 1.6(a), Core Business includes everything provided to hospitals, physicians or healthcare entities — essentially all of the 1.2 Business — so the concession promised for 8.4 terminations may be illusory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare acknowledgment of reasonableness; it states a conclusion rather than a testable obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Article VII's assumption that the restrictions may be "overbroad or unenforceable" and require judicial modification, a mild internal tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional representation with a closed three-item list and an "as disclosed in writing" carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.8 preserves a separate Non-Competition Agreement of even date, which limb (iii) would otherwise cover, though the "except for this Agreement" opener partly covers it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard no-conflict representation; nothing vague enough to fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.1 and 9.8; no contrary provision located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause protects "the provisions of Articles I, IV or V" — Article I is only the definitions, so the intended reference to Article III (Confidential Information) has been mis-typed twice, and it invokes "the Company's rights under Article VII hereof", which is this very Article.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mis-numbering means the equitable-relief remedy on its face does not reach breaches of Article III, which 3.1 and 3.2 plainly intend to protect, and the same mis-citation recurs in 8.2(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the earliest of the third anniversary ... or the first to occur of the events" is clumsy but its effect is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It lines up with 1.9's Employment Term and with the five termination routes in 8.2-8.5; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (c) cites "Articles I, IV, V or VI" where Article III was clearly meant, limb (d) begins with a stray "or", and "conduct causing ... substantial public disgrace or disrepute" is inherently vague; the cure right refers to "such failure" though most Cause events are not failures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The notice-and-cure sentence is hard to square with instantaneous Cause events like a felony conviction, and the mis-citation to Article I repeats the error in Article VII.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "substantially failed to perform his essential duties ... for one hundred twenty (120) days in any two hundred forty (240) day period" is workable, but "except as expressly set forth in this Section" against the sweeping no-other-bonus sentence is awkward.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves the Reorganization Bonus "in accordance with Section 2.2(e)", but the Reorganization Bonus is 2.2(f) and 2.2(e) is Commissions — a plain cross-reference error carried into the payout mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the compensation at the rate or level, as applicable, in effect on the date of such termination" does not say whether it means Base Salary alone or salary plus Allowance, Bonus and Commissions, and "less any amounts owing by the Employee" is an open set-off.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its second sentence lets the Employee terminate "for any other reason pursuant to this Section 8.4" while 8.5 governs voluntary resignation, and it again cites "Section 2.2(e)" for the Reorganization Bonus defined in 2.2(f).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "effective as of a date chosen by the Company, however, no later than thirty (30) business days" gives the Company unilateral control over the effective date of the Employee's own resignation, phrased loosely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4 already grants the Employee a right to terminate "for any other reason pursuant to this Section 8.4", so which section governs a no-reason resignation — and therefore whether severance is owed — is genuinely uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate headings clause with no operative bite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere relies on headings for meaning.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard severability; "in whole or in part" is clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article VII's final sentence directs judicial modification of overbroad restrictions rather than severance, so the two salvage mechanisms differ for Article V.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence never requires a waiver to be in writing, yet the second refers to "such written waiver", a drafting gap; the clause also protects only the Company's rights.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.8 requires modifications to be in writing and executed by all parties, which partly fills the gap but does not match the waiver language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The permitted assignments are enumerated with the limiting word "only", leaving little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Company" means Ajuba and Ajuba India together, so a merger of one but not the other raises a fit question, and 8.4's payment obligations run to Ajuba India specifically.
